import Mathlib.Analysis.Real.Sqrt
import Mathlib.Tactic.FieldSimp
import Mathlib.Tactic.Linarith
import Mathlib.Tactic.Ring

/-!+# A deterministic bound for a normalized bad mass

Zhou–Suzuki, arXiv:2611.05813v1, §6.4, Fact 12, equation (60).
The source is CC BY 4.0; this is an original Lean implementation of its scalar proof.
The consumer is the following proof of Theorem 7 with `g = Z_good / M` and
`b = Z_bad / M`. No assertion about those random quantities or their moments
is made here. Positive total mass rules out the zero-denominator convention.
-/

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Analysis.NormalizedMass

/-- The bad fraction is bounded by bad mass plus square-root error, and then by
bad mass plus quadratic error. These are both inequalities of source Fact 12.
The source's nonnegativity condition on `b` is retained even though the first
square identity already holds for real `b` whenever the total mass is positive.
Neither individual mass is required to be strictly positive. -/
theorem bad_mass_ratio_bounds {g b : ℝ} (hg : 0 ≤ g) (hb : 0 ≤ b) (hpos : 0 < g + b) :
    b / (g + b) ≤ b + (1 - Real.sqrt g) ^ 2 ∧
      b + (1 - Real.sqrt g) ^ 2 ≤ b + (1 - g) ^ 2 := by
  have hs := Real.sqrt_nonneg g
  have hs2 := Real.sq_sqrt hg
  constructor
  · have hdiff : b + (1 - Real.sqrt g) ^ 2 - b / (g + b) =
        (g + b - Real.sqrt g) ^ 2 / (g + b) := by
      field_simp
      ring_nf
      rw [hs2]
      ring
    apply sub_nonneg.mp
    rw [hdiff]
    exact div_nonneg (sq_nonneg _) hpos.le
  · have hden : 0 < 1 + Real.sqrt g := by linarith
    have hfactor : (1 - Real.sqrt g) * (1 + Real.sqrt g) = 1 - g := by
      nlinarith [hs2]
    have hid : (1 - Real.sqrt g) ^ 2 = (1 - g) ^ 2 / (1 + Real.sqrt g) ^ 2 := by
      apply (eq_div_iff (pow_ne_zero 2 hden.ne')).2
      rw [← mul_pow, hfactor]
    apply add_le_add le_rfl
    rw [hid]
    exact div_le_self (sq_nonneg _) (by nlinarith)

end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Analysis.NormalizedMass

lesson.title: Control a bad fraction without dividing by good mass alone

sources.label: Zhou–Suzuki, Fact 12, §6.4, Eq. (60)
sources.scope: Complete deterministic fact only; Theorem 7's random-mass application remains separate

assumptions: g and b are arbitrary nonnegative real numbers; their sum is strictly positive.
The square root is the nonnegative real square root. Either individual mass may vanish.
lesson.statement: The fraction of bad mass is at most the unnormalized bad mass plus the squared deviation of the square root of good mass from one. This is in turn at most bad mass plus the squared deviation of good mass from one.

steps.title: Identify the safe denominator
steps.text: Put t=g+b. The hypothesis t>0 allows ordinary real division and gives a nonnegative square divided by t. We never divide by g, which could be zero. Let s be the nonnegative square root of g, so s²=g.
steps.lean: hpos supplies positive total mass; Real.sqrt_nonneg and Real.sq_sqrt give hs and hs2. No random-variable structure is involved.

steps.title: Write the error as a nonnegative square
steps.text: Subtract the bad fraction from the proposed upper bound. Combining b/t with 1 uses t-b=g. The result is exactly a square divided by t, proving the first inequality with coefficient one.
steps.lean: hdiff proves this identity by field_simp, ring_nf and hs2; div_nonneg and sq_nonneg prove its sign. sub_nonneg.mp turns the difference back into the desired inequality.

steps.title: Replace square-root error by quadratic error
steps.text: Factor 1-g=(1-s)(1+s). Because s≥0, the second factor is positive and its square is at least one. Divide the squared factorization by (1+s)² and use that dividing a nonnegative quantity by a number at least one cannot increase it. Add the same b to both sides.
steps.lean: hden, hfactor and hid express the positivity and factorization. eq_div_iff and mul_pow justify division; div_le_self gives the comparison, and add_le_add preserves it after adding b.

lesson.lean_statement: Universal real parameters, three explicit source hypotheses and a conjunction of the two inequalities. Real division is totalized, but hpos guarantees its ordinary nonzero-denominator meaning here.
lesson.lean_proof: The two branches of constructor correspond to the two source inequalities. Every denominator/sign condition is proved internally from the stated hypotheses. The intentionally retained source hypothesis hb triggers an unused-variable warning; it is not a missing proof or an additional assumption.
